main.title: Boktai: The Sun Is in Your Hand
main.subtitle: The cartridge asks for sunlight
main.summary: Boktai: The Sun Is in Your Hand is Konami's Game Boy Advance action role-playing adventure about Django, a young vampire hunter carrying the Gun Del Sol. A light sensor built into the cartridge measures real sunlight and connects the player's surroundings with the energy available inside the game. Produced by Hideo Kojima, the adventure makes that physical relationship part of its identity rather than an optional accessory. Hunting the undead requires attention to the world beyond the screen, because the light falling on the handheld can affect the tools available to its hero.

cards.heading: The cartridge asks for sunlight
cards.text: Boktai: The Sun Is in Your Hand is Konami's Game Boy Advance action role-playing adventure about Django, a young vampire hunter carrying the Gun Del Sol. A light sensor built into the cartridge measures real sunlight and connects the player's surroundings with the energy available inside the game. Produced by Hideo Kojima, the adventure makes that physical relationship part of its identity rather than an optional accessory. Hunting the undead requires attention to the world beyond the screen, because the light falling on the handheld can affect the tools available to its hero.

cards.heading: The gun can run out of daylight
cards.text: The Gun Del Sol stores the energy gathered through the sensor, allowing Django to spend that reserve during an encounter. When it is exhausted and no sunlight is available, avoiding enemies becomes important until a Solar Station can provide another charge. The physical resource therefore changes the immediate choices inside the adventure. A player carrying a well-prepared weapon can confront a threat directly, while the same route may call for caution when the reserve is low. The sensor affects how the hunter approaches a situation rather than simply changing a decorative meter.

cards.heading: The time of day reaches the landscape
cards.text: Setting the local time and time zone lets the game estimate sunrise and sunset, connecting its fictional day with the player's location. The surroundings respond through details such as morning birds and an orange glow toward evening. Sunlight can also help restore a Solar Tree damaged by the darkness surrounding the Immortals. These effects extend the cartridge's central idea beyond firing the gun. The light outside becomes part of both the hunter's practical resources and the condition of a world whose changing atmosphere follows the passage of the real day.

main.title: R-Type Final
main.subtitle: One more mission against the Bydo
main.summary: R-Type Final is Irem's PlayStation 2 horizontally scrolling shooter, first released in Japan on 17 July 2003. A pilot investigates the remains of an earlier battle before returning to the long war against the Bydo. The player advances through hostile stages in a small craft whose weapons and attached Force device determine how each danger can be approached. The title was intended as a farewell to the main series. Its stages, unlockable ships and accompanying fragments of writing turn that last mission into a survey of the strange universe R-Type had built.

cards.heading: One more mission against the Bydo
cards.text: R-Type Final is Irem's PlayStation 2 horizontally scrolling shooter, first released in Japan on 17 July 2003. A pilot investigates the remains of an earlier battle before returning to the long war against the Bydo. The player advances through hostile stages in a small craft whose weapons and attached Force device determine how each danger can be approached. The title was intended as a farewell to the main series. Its stages, unlockable ships and accompanying fragments of writing turn that last mission into a survey of the strange universe R-Type had built.

cards.heading: Give the same danger another machine
cards.text: Different craft and weapon arrangements change the options available against a familiar pattern. The Force can shield a vulnerable direction or extend an attack, making its position part of the player's response rather than an automatic accessory. Learning a stage involves recognising where a threat appears and deciding which part of the equipment should answer it. Unlocking additional ships gives that knowledge another use: a route already understood can be attempted with different strengths and limitations. The collection becomes a practical invitation to revisit the same hostile space.

cards.heading: A final title that became a new beginning
cards.text: Kazuma Kujo produced and designed the game, with Yuki Iwai composing the score. The campaign contains alternative routes and outcomes, giving its apparent conclusion more than one direction. North American and European editions followed in 2004. Despite the original intention behind its name, the series continued in other forms and eventually returned to scrolling action with R-Type Final 2 in 2021. The PlayStation 2 release retains the character of a retrospective farewell, gathering many machines and ideas around another attempt to understand and survive the Bydo.

main.title: Downhill Domination
main.subtitle: The whole mountain becomes a racecourse
main.summary: Downhill Domination is Incog Inc. Entertainment's PlayStation 2 mountain-bike racing game, first released in North America on 22 July 2003. Riders descend large courses at exaggerated speed, taking jumps and exchanging blows while trying to reach the finish first. The mountain offers room to choose a line rather than keeping everyone inside a narrow circuit. A shortcut may promise an advantage while bringing a more difficult landing. The game's arcade approach turns downhill riding into a mixture of route finding, spectacle and the immediate problem of staying ahead of another cyclist.

cards.heading: The whole mountain becomes a racecourse
cards.text: Downhill Domination is Incog Inc. Entertainment's PlayStation 2 mountain-bike racing game, first released in North America on 22 July 2003. Riders descend large courses at exaggerated speed, taking jumps and exchanging blows while trying to reach the finish first. The mountain offers room to choose a line rather than keeping everyone inside a narrow circuit. A shortcut may promise an advantage while bringing a more difficult landing. The game's arcade approach turns downhill riding into a mixture of route finding, spectacle and the immediate problem of staying ahead of another cyclist.

cards.heading: A fast descent leaves little time to reconsider
cards.text: The player has to read the slope ahead while managing speed, jumps and nearby rivals. Tricks add another reason to leave the ground, but a good-looking movement still needs a safe landing if the descent is to continue. Contact with opponents makes the surrounding race more than background scenery. Career progression opens more riders and equipment, while repeated attempts reveal where the terrain offers a better route. The same mountain gradually becomes easier to read, allowing the player to commit to a line earlier and carry more speed through it.

cards.heading: Fictional racers meet the real sport
cards.text: The initial cast of invented riders is joined by unlockable professionals, including Eric Carter, Tara Llanes, Brian Lopes, Richie Schley and Missy Giove. Their presence connects the exaggerated action to downhill cycling beyond the game. Scott Campbell directed and designed the project for Incog, with Sony publishing in North America and Codemasters bringing it to Europe in 2004. Multiplayer makes the descent a shared competition. Its identity comes from enlarging the sport's dangers into an arcade race while retaining the basic excitement of choosing a path down a mountain at speed.

main.title: Shining Soul II
main.subtitle: Choose a hero and enter the dungeon
main.summary: Shining Soul II is Grasshopper Manufacture's Game Boy Advance action role-playing game built around exploring dungeons, fighting in real time and developing a chosen character. Eight classes provide different starting abilities and equipment choices, while a link cable allows companions to join the expedition. The Shining setting becomes the home of a compact loot-driven adventure, where another weapon or improved skill can change how the next room is approached. Its appeal develops through repeated expeditions, connecting the immediate rhythm of an attack with the longer process of building a capable individual hero.

cards.heading: Choose a hero and enter the dungeon
cards.text: Shining Soul II is Grasshopper Manufacture's Game Boy Advance action role-playing game built around exploring dungeons, fighting in real time and developing a chosen character. Eight classes provide different starting abilities and equipment choices, while a link cable allows companions to join the expedition. The Shining setting becomes the home of a compact loot-driven adventure, where another weapon or improved skill can change how the next room is approached. Its appeal develops through repeated expeditions, connecting the immediate rhythm of an attack with the longer process of building a capable individual hero.

cards.heading: The same weapon can suit a different class
cards.text: Classes differ in their use of equipment as well as their available skills. A spear can be used as a thrusting weapon by a Warrior or thrown by an Archer, giving the same general item another practical role in a different character's hands. Skills, spells and attributes offer further ways to develop the chosen class. The player can switch between equipped weapons and useful items while exploring. Preparation therefore involves more than collecting higher numbers, because the class determines how that equipment actually behaves during an encounter with the enemies ahead.

cards.heading: A charged attack creates another opening
cards.text: Holding the attack button prepares a stronger action, while ordinary strikes provide a quicker response. A Soul item can also be charged through defeating enemies and released for a special effect. These options give a familiar dungeon routine several decisions about timing and resources. Cooperative play adds the possibility of bringing different classes into the same expedition, allowing their strengths to complement one another. The continuing supply of equipment and experience gives each outing a result beyond reaching its final room, preparing the character for another attempt with a different set of practical options.

main.title: F-Zero GX
main.summary: F-Zero GX is a 2003 racing game developed by Amusement Vision, a division of Sega, and published by Nintendo for the GameCube.

cards.heading: F-Zero GX
cards.text: F-Zero GX is a 2003 racing game developed by Amusement Vision, a division of Sega, and published by Nintendo for the GameCube. It was released in Japan on July 25, 2003, North America on August 25, Australia on October 24, and Europe on October 31. Sega also released an arcade version, F-Zero AX, which uses the Triforce arcade system board.

cards.heading: Nine chapters for Captain Falcon
cards.text: F-Zero GX retains the high-speed gameplay of the previous F-Zero games, with an emphasis on track memorization and reflexes. It introduces a "story mode", in which the player completes missions as Captain Falcon through nine chapters.

cards.heading: Nintendo and Sega build a demanding racer
cards.text: The project was the first significant game collaboration between Nintendo and Sega. It runs on an enhanced version of the game engine used in Super Monkey Ball (2001). GX received positive reviews for its visuals, intense action, sense of speed, and track design, though its difficulty was criticized. In 2025, it was rereleased on the Nintendo Classics service for the Nintendo Switch 2.

main.title: Mario Golf: Toadstool Tour
main.subtitle: Camelot · GameCube
main.summary: Mario Golf: Toadstool Tour is Camelot's GameCube golf game, combining Mario characters with courses that move from recognisable fairways toward more fantastical Mushroom Kingdom terrain. The aim remains to finish each hole in as few strokes as possible. Character statistics influence power, control and the height of a shot, making the selection of golfer part of the approach. The player studies distance, wind and the landing area before using a timed power meter to turn that plan into a particular stroke.

cards.heading: Read the course before choosing the club
cards.text: Mario Golf: Toadstool Tour is Camelot's GameCube golf game, combining Mario characters with courses that move from recognisable fairways toward more fantastical Mushroom Kingdom terrain. The aim remains to finish each hole in as few strokes as possible. Character statistics influence power, control and the height of a shot, making the selection of golfer part of the approach. The player studies distance, wind and the landing area before using a timed power meter to turn that plan into a particular stroke.

cards.heading: A familiar obstacle becomes a golfing hazard
cards.text: Later courses introduce features such as Chain Chomps, lava and pipes, placing Mario's world inside the practical problem of finding a safe route to the hole. Spin changes how a ball behaves after landing, while automatic and manual shots offer different balances of assistance and risk. A useful stroke is therefore more than a successful timing input. The ball must arrive somewhere that leaves the next attempt manageable, and a stronger shot can be less valuable than a carefully chosen position on a difficult green.

cards.heading: Another challenge on the same fairway
cards.text: Ring Attack adds hoops to pass through while meeting a score requirement, asking the player to reconsider the familiar layout. Character matches and tournaments open further rewards, while connection with Mario Golf: Advance Tour links the home-console game to its Game Boy Advance companion. Motoi Sakuraba composed the music. Released in 2003, Toadstool Tour builds its variety through the relationship between a consistent swing system and increasingly expressive courses. Learning the controls creates a foundation; reading what a particular hole asks of those controls supplies the continuing game.

main.title: Pokémon Pinball: Ruby & Sapphire
main.subtitle: A Poké Ball takes the place of the ball
main.summary: Pokémon Pinball: Ruby & Sapphire is Jupiter's Game Boy Advance pinball game adapting the creatures and world of Pokémon Ruby and Sapphire into two themed tables. Keeping the ball in play produces points, while special modes turn successful shots into attempts to catch and evolve Pokémon. The collection gives the score chase another continuing purpose, with a Pokédex recording the creatures obtained across sessions. Familiar characters become parts of the table's machinery and targets, making the pinball layout another way of exploring a region already associated with travelling and collecting companions.

cards.heading: A Poké Ball takes the place of the ball
cards.text: Pokémon Pinball: Ruby & Sapphire is Jupiter's Game Boy Advance pinball game adapting the creatures and world of Pokémon Ruby and Sapphire into two themed tables. Keeping the ball in play produces points, while special modes turn successful shots into attempts to catch and evolve Pokémon. The collection gives the score chase another continuing purpose, with a Pokédex recording the creatures obtained across sessions. Familiar characters become parts of the table's machinery and targets, making the pinball layout another way of exploring a region already associated with travelling and collecting companions.

cards.heading: A catch requires the right shots
cards.text: Catching a Pokémon is connected with activating a mode and completing its objectives while continuing to control the ball. The player has to direct shots toward useful targets without losing the basic rhythm of keeping the ball above the flippers. The two tables provide different arrangements and available encounters, giving the choice of table a consequence beyond its appearance. A successful catch therefore becomes a small sequence inside the larger run, asking for focused control at the moment when the opportunity to add another creature has finally been made available.

cards.heading: Another run can add to the collection
cards.text: The Pokédex provides a record that lasts beyond an individual score attempt, allowing a shorter session to achieve something through a new catch or evolution. Bonus challenges vary the action between periods on the main table. The combination gives different players different reasons to continue: a high score can remain the immediate aim, while the collection supplies a longer project assembled through repeated encounters. Ruby & Sapphire retains the recognisable skill of pinball, but gives its targets identities that make a particular successful shot memorable after the ball has finally been lost.

main.title: Dungeons & Dragons: Heroes
main.subtitle: Four heroes return to an unfinished struggle
main.summary: Dungeons & Dragons: Heroes is Atari's Xbox action role-playing game, first released in North America on 16 September 2003. Four adventurers are brought back to life to face Kaedin, the wizard whose final spell killed them after their earlier victory. A dwarf cleric, elf wizard, halfling rogue and human fighter supply the party's different roles. The player travels through a campaign built around fighting, equipment and character development, either alone or with companions. The tabletop setting provides creatures and fantasy identities for an adventure designed around immediate, shared console action.

cards.heading: Four heroes return to an unfinished struggle
cards.text: Dungeons & Dragons: Heroes is Atari's Xbox action role-playing game, first released in North America on 16 September 2003. Four adventurers are brought back to life to face Kaedin, the wizard whose final spell killed them after their earlier victory. A dwarf cleric, elf wizard, halfling rogue and human fighter supply the party's different roles. The player travels through a campaign built around fighting, equipment and character development, either alone or with companions. The tabletop setting provides creatures and fantasy identities for an adventure designed around immediate, shared console action.

cards.heading: Let the party change without interrupting the adventure
cards.text: Up to four players can join or leave during play, and characters of different levels can travel together. Each class brings its own abilities to the group, while levelling supplies points and skills that can be assigned after the immediate fight is over. The system keeps character development connected to the action without demanding a pause in the middle of every encounter. Familiar Dungeons & Dragons monsters give the party a recognisable sequence of threats. Cooperation grows from making the available roles useful together as the group crosses another room or confronts a stronger enemy.

cards.heading: A tabletop world becomes a living-room expedition
cards.text: The campaign sends the revived heroes after Planar Gems tied to different planes of existence, giving the journey a structure of exploration and recovered power. Four difficulty levels extend the challenge, with Nightmare becoming available after completing Hard. Gary Spinrad composed the score, and Glenn Fabry supplied the cover artwork. Heroes uses the Dungeons & Dragons name to support an accessible action adventure rather than reproduce the full tabletop rules. Its central pleasure is the continuity of the party, allowing friends to enter the expedition, develop their characters and keep moving through the same fantasy world together.

main.title: The Simpsons: Hit & Run
main.summary: The Simpsons: Hit & Run is a 2003 action-adventure game developed by Radical Entertainment and published by Vivendi Universal Games.

cards.heading: The Simpsons: Hit & Run
cards.text: The Simpsons: Hit & Run is a 2003 action-adventure game developed by Radical Entertainment and published by Vivendi Universal Games. It is based on the American animated television series The Simpsons, and is the 22nd installment in The Simpsons series of video games.

cards.heading: A conspiracy spreads through Springfield
cards.text: It follows the Simpson family and their friend Apu Nahasapeemapetilon as they witness many strange incidents that occur in Springfield; security cameras, mysterious vans, crop circles, and a "new and improved" flavour of the popular soft drink Buzz Cola that causes insanity. Taking matters into their own hands, they discover numerous shocking secrets, and soon realise these incidents are part of a larger alien conspiracy, caused by Kang and Kodos. The gameplay largely focuses on varied missions; players often race enemies and interact with supporting characters on timed quests, as well as engaging in side tasks and exploring Springfield.

cards.heading: Building Springfield with the show's creators
cards.text: Development of The Simpsons: Hit & Run began in late 2001 as a spiritual successor to Radical Entertainment's previous game The Simpsons: Road Rage (2001). Production was extensive, as the team sought to differentiate it from Road Rage, deeming that their new entry in the franchise required a different direction. It was heavily inspired by the Grand Theft Auto series, and the development team re-purposed the open world design and nuanced character development for the game. This encouraged collaboration with the show's writers and its cast, who helped to craft the story and dialogue. It was released in North America on September 16, 2003, and in Europe on October 21, 2003, for the GameCube, PlayStation 2 and Xbox. It was ported to Windows in North America on November 11, 2003, and in Europe on November 21, 2003.

cards.heading: A successful Simpsons adaptation
cards.text: The game received positive reviews from critics, who particularly praised its interpretation of The Simpsons as a video game, as well as its parodical take on Grand Theft Auto III (2001) and graphics; criticism mostly surrounded some aspects of gameplay, such as bugs and glitches. Often considered to be the best Simpsons tie-in game, Hit & Run was also a commercial success, with recorded sales of over 3 million worldwide by June 2007. It received the award for Fave Video Game at the 2004 Nickelodeon Australian Kids' Choice Awards. On the PlayStation 2, GameCube, and Xbox, it earned Greatest Hits, Player's Choice, and Platinum Hits respectively.

main.title: Voodoo Vince
main.subtitle: The hero's misfortune becomes his strongest attack
main.summary: Voodoo Vince is Beep Industries' Xbox platform game, released in North America on 23 September 2003. Its hero is a voodoo doll whose ability to hurt nearby enemies depends on the trouble inflicted on himself. Familiar jumping, punching and spinning establish the basic movement, while special powers turn comic accidents into attacks. The setting and Steve Kirk's music give the journey a distinctive character. The central joke also supplies a practical rule: the dangerous object in the room may be something Vince needs to use rather than simply avoid.

cards.heading: The hero's misfortune becomes his strongest attack
cards.text: Voodoo Vince is Beep Industries' Xbox platform game, released in North America on 23 September 2003. Its hero is a voodoo doll whose ability to hurt nearby enemies depends on the trouble inflicted on himself. Familiar jumping, punching and spinning establish the basic movement, while special powers turn comic accidents into attacks. The setting and Steve Kirk's music give the journey a distinctive character. The central joke also supplies a practical rule: the dangerous object in the room may be something Vince needs to use rather than simply avoid.

cards.heading: Find a useful way to suffer
cards.text: Enemies leave beads that fill Vince's power meter, allowing a special attack once it is ready. These powers injure the doll in different theatrical ways while destroying nearby opponents. Environmental puzzles take the idea further by asking the player to activate something capable of harming Vince at the right place. Collectibles improve health, lives and the number of powers available. The player moves between ordinary platforming and situations where understanding the joke reveals the solution, recognising how the surroundings can turn the hero's apparent vulnerability into an advantage.

cards.heading: A handmade character with a musical sense of place
cards.text: Clayton Kauzlaric directed the game, whose levels also include vehicles and short departures from standard platforming. Steve Kirk's score helps connect the varied locations through a consistent musical voice. A remastered edition reached Xbox One and Windows in 2017, making the adventure available again after its original Xbox release. The design remains memorable because its unusual premise reaches beyond the character's appearance. Vince's stitched body explains the attacks, the puzzles and the comedy, allowing the game to build an entire journey around a single recognisable physical idea.
